chapterTitle: Chapter 3: Synaptic Memoriam of a steel fossil shell
editorText:
“Captain, the cavity is just up ahead, 20 meters out”. John slowed his pace to a quiet walk upon Tao’s announcement, the others meeting his pace. They were silent, rolling their feet onto the ground as they walked so no sudden cracks from the rock bed beneath them might announce their presence. Their suit’s heel’s articulated with every tendon’s pull and ease. “2 meters” Tao whispered. John looked ahead but saw nothing. He wasn’t surprised though given what had just transpired. He knew the technology's capabilities. “It should be right here” Tao’s words gently flowed from her mouth as heat expelled from her helmet’s exhaust vents. A cold wind rose from silence stirring around them, a small howl erupted, ripping through the valley stirring up snow from the ground, shedding any stray icicles to thin from the cliff's face.

“Our suit’s power reserves cores have been exhausted, We won’t last much longer out here in the cold”. In response John raised his hand to hip height, his fingers splayed out level with the ground. He was silent, still, the others waited with anticipation. He took two more steps closer still with his left shoulder to the cliff face. He raised his rifle barrel then poked the cliff face with his rifle muzzle, although as he suspected his muzzle didn’t meet the sound of crunching steel against rock, but the soft static crackle that he had heard when the debris fell through their own Mesh. His muzzle dipped into the cliff like a stick in a still pool of water. “This is it” John stepped back, ice crushing beneath his heel as his weight sunk into the piling snow. “Your up techy!”,

Tau knelt down into the snow crushing it beneath her,gleaning into her wrist terminal. “Prepping echo” She took a moment to think then began tapping away again “Annnnd.. that should do it!” her voice seemed a little less confident this time but confident enough. “Confirm flight plan” pulsed on her wrist terminal. “What’s the hold up” said John “I needed to set a recorded flight path for the time I’ll pilot it manually through the Mesh. Once on the other side I’ll lose comms due to the sound barrier, it will finish it’s scan then return to the recorded flight paths final origin then exit, I just threw the vectors in reverse so it comes out when comes back to the other side of the Mesh. “Oo k” Said John, pretending to understand. “it should stop recording a second after it enters the mesh or loses comms either way we will get her back” Tao seemed more confident now she had reassured herself it seemed. Shai looked back at Tex, Tex shrugged his shoulders.

“Deploying Echo” Tao moved smoothly in her actions. From the rear of her suit’s shoulder blade, the same port the peregrine had ejected from slid open, each blade which formed the port window retracting within the suit’s armoured shell. Everything about the port seal had been carefully crafted. The edges of the seal blades pushed outward against the edge of the next blade, meaning that any positive pressure from within the suit would force a seal in a vacuum environment, making it user friendly in space. Shai found her confidence in the Mark IV increasing as she observed the intricate operation. Before John had even given a thought to what could possibly lie behind the mesh, a light whisper hummed over his shoulder. A small drone no larger than the size of a rhinoceros beetle buzzed past vanishing into the mesh consumed by the cliff face as the ripples from it’s wake dissipated in microseconds into an illusion. To the human eye the small glitch in the mesh couldn’t be seen. Only visible really by the high frequency echo location scanners performed by sonic sensors. A trained engineer might pick up on the pattern, although to anyone else.. it appeared merely as instrument sound without proper curve fitting transforms. Tao had proven this earlier. The inbuilt autopilot program of the Echo had not been designed to detect these “light mesh” instances yet alone pass through them.

“I’ve lost contact with the drone”, said Tao tapping away on her terminal, her suit activating sentry mode as she became occupied with the task ahead. “What’s the hold up” John was getting impatient, “We wait for the data link when it gets back”, “How”, Tao intervened “I’d say a minute at most”. Tex and Shai were huddled together up against the cliff face. “Starting to Prune up in this Dam suit” Tex groaned moving in discomfort. “Big guy wants some action” Chuckled Shai softly under her voice.

“Careful what you wish for”. Tao had a certain unease in her tone, her head fixed still in her wrist terminal. “My suits long range scanners have picked up the engine signature of the LRD from earlier” This time she was less calm, but still controlled. “Persistent fucker!” Said John, “I thought we shook that thing already”, “It’s Engineer probably picked up on the impulse anomaly I detected earlier” Tao flicked her HUD view to the others. “It’s turned around for a second run, heading our way”

“We’re sitting ducks here”, Said John as he nodded over at Tex triggering him to reach for his Railstorm. “Power reserve for hard light mesh will only give us about 10 seconds of concealment Cap” Kitten had understood the stress in John’s tone anticipating his question before he’d even asked.

the charging of coils let out a winding high pitched humm. Tex mounted the Railstorm on his shoulder. His eyes fixated through the targeting reticle on the ridge lying in wait for the drone’s return run.

“20 seconds John till we’re in short range scanners”. Tau seemed calm more than the others. “I think I’d rather take my chances with what's on the other side”, said John, “Second that” said Tex, still with his sites locked on the ridge above. A second later a crackling static let out startling John. He stood back locking his sites on the the ripples of where echo had just zipped out of. Echo had emerged from the mesh unscathed, it stopped, pivoted on it’s axis then headed straight towards Tau. Like a friendly companion it tapped it’s docking bay on the back of her suit then re-coupled with it’s landing arm. The arm drew the drone back into Tau’s suit ready to be deployed again. “Collating the data, I need a few seconds”. “Get it done” John seemed collected, but you could hear the grinding in his tone alone. A frustration of silence lingered among the others as tension built in the air. “The structure inside seems natural but.. scans picked up heartbeat harmonics of a life-form..  it appears to be.. human”. John turned his head to Shai, confused more than concerned “I’ll take my chances with a human over an assault Drone”. John’s rifle muzzle dipped into the cliff wall like a like a drop entering a pool. ripples rose up humming from the entry point with a wave of crackling static. As he stepped through the mesh his body gradually disappeared swallowed by the cliff face leaving behind a silent wisp. The static crackling stopped.

Tao, Shai and Tex all filed in behind where John had just entered, Tex walking backwards letting the suit’s suggested kinematics pairing with Shai. The formed retreat closed out the sky ridges tightly as Tex’s shoulder turrets watched in opposing directions gyrating along the walls seamlessly. The hum down of Tex’s Railstorm cells brought the tunnel to a silence. Charged hydrogen focused light beams packed enough electrons in the punch to disable any incoming drone within milliseconds. Tao had worked on the development of the charging system herself, although she kept this to herself.

Shai was busy looking at her HUD’s life form signatures within their proximity watching for any unwanted visitors. “John, that life form echo picked up I’m running it through the computer”, “That LRD will be at the mesh by now not far behind us” said Tau abruptly. “We should keep moving” said John. “We don’t know how, inquisitive our old friend will be”. He raised his sites moving forward in a smooth motion. After a few steps into the tunnels depths a beam of red light shot out scanning the wall directly in front of him, his armours outline shadowed on the wall within the scan print, Whatever it was, he was in it’s sites, he knew this It wasn’t his rifles targeting laser or any of the others scanning arrays it was too large. John stopped dead in his tracks taking to the ground immediately. “Take cover!” The red cone of lasers flickered past him deeper into the tunnel. John turned around on the ground, aiming his sites at the direction of the tunnel entrance. An explosion erupted through the cave sending rocks and debris on his back and pummelling directly into the others who were now huddled against the tunnel walls where what small crevasses offered minimal protection. John didn’t hesitate, returning fire at the large metallic monstrosities sensor dish. Sparks flew from the drone around it’s shell as what remained of it’s rear slowly emerged through the hard light mesh. The heavily armoured assault sparrow forced it’s way deeper scraping the tunnel walls in it’s wake to the sound of grinding steel and rock. “It must have detected the curtain breaks in the mesh when we entered the cave” shouted Tau.

They had nowhere to go. If they stepped out that would be the end. John’s shoulder turrets were both firing rapidly, sending a barrage of fire at the drone scattering any proper reading it could make out ahead. “I can only suppress it for so long, it’s armour is too thick… Tex!” Shouted John. Tex  reached back over his shoulder and retrieved his Storm Rail. He clenching his fist around the Storm rail’s handle waiting for a break in the curtain of fire. “Hold fire” Kitten chimed in an almost complete calm monotone pleasantly easing the tension as John and his team regained their focus. The LRD was at a stand still, re-priming it’s cannon, echoes of charging wires hummed through the tunnel.  The sound of Tex’s Railstorm charging had complimented that of the Drones, He wouldn’t let it have a chance to open fire again. Collected he stepped out with the drone clear in his Storm Rail’s site. His would sing first and have the final clap as it’s coils let out a loud clap through the tunnel behind him.

The drone shuddered in it’s place moving from side to side crashing into the walls, disoriented  like a drunken belter trying to find his way home from the star bar. It moaned in electronic groans and splutters, as it’s main turret powered down.

“It still has it’s kinetic turret!” Tau was trying to contain herself, sweat ran down her forehead as the held back the images from her blown apart comrades that took blows from rail rifles in the previous war. It wasn’t pretty watching your closest friend be ripped in two, their organs splayed out on the ground by a 12 inch thick iron slug leaving an unscheduled painting along the hull of an Icarus. She knew that while they might survive most shock penetrations now with the new suit’s built nervous network, in the moment they would not be able to recover to finish the job.

“It’s video feeds are disabled but I’m still picking up a sounding scan”, Tau held her breath, speaking quietly. Their Mark IV suit’s dampened out any internal sounds, but instinct still took over as though they were hiding their frail exposed bodies, Shai turned her attention to her heartbeat scanner heightening the tension in her voice. “Aah guys, that life form I picked up earlier it’s getting closer, it’s coming from the other side of the tunnel, We’ll be pinched”. Tex began reaching for a slug to load into the Railstorm’s kinetic chamber. “Whatever it is, it’s not going to like what I’ve got in store”, “Stay where you are Tex! That drone can still turn you to pink mist!” said Tau frantically, Tex chambered the slug in his Storm rail then hugged his back hard up against the tunnel wall.

“The signal.. it appears to be human”, Said Shai. She looked up at Tex from the other side of the tunnel, her voice edged mixed with relief to confusion. “It’s… it’s getting closer, 20 meters and closing on our 6”. John remained fixed in position, prone his sites perched still fixed on the drones direction. His shoulder turret pivoted 180 degrees covering the rear of the tunnel behind them. “I got it covered, we have bigger problems right now, focus on that fucking drone…” Said John.

Everything was quiet, awkwardly quiet. The Sparrow hovered vigilantly, fixed, waiting for a positive read to be picked up on one of John’s team. “It’s operating on Autopilot” Tau began to explain but more for herself than anything “It must have lost contact with command when it crossed the mesh barrier” She whispered, then the tunnel fell to silence once more. The walls began to vibrate and hum, like the mountain was becoming alive, gently. A loud thud shook the tunnel sending rubble and debris clamouring over their armoured suit’s. An ensemble of metallic clangs as their suit’s took the grunt of the falling debris announced their positions even more.

“It’s trying to echo-locate us!” said John. “Fuck this!” said Tex, reluctant to stand there like a rabbit in the headlight. They all knew the sparrow would soon determine their positions with it’s advanced AI, differentiating the sound of rubble against steel would be no hard feat. Tex had waited long enough in his mind, He selected the highest charge possible on the Rail Storm, and listened to the purr of the  coils as they began to prime, just enough, then kneeled down in the open of the tunnel, Storm Rail at the ready, converging his targeting reticle on the sparrows main processing unit. “Covering Fire!” yelled John. Instantly Tau pivoted from the left side of the tunnel just off to the front left of Tex raising her rifle as she did in a smooth motion. The spacing was tight between them, with just enough opening for John to lay down fire between Tex and Tau, an unconventional and completely unorthodox manoeuvre by any training standard, but what choice did they have?

A barrage of fire opened up toward the Sparrow as soon as John had gave the order. Sparks of splintering, hot molten amber ricochet off the armour cladded drone as John and Taus Sherpa rounds did nothing to damage the drone. It was akin to throwing sand in the face of the schoolyard bully, only delaying a heavy handed punch to the face. The sparrows sensor arrays lit up, overwhelmed by molten rain, it’s scans became completely useless. Tex watched on anxiously, as the Storm Rail hummed while it charged for it’s next shot, seconds felt like days, as he willed the last bar of the charge gauge in his HUD to green light him so he could let all hell loose. Tex’s sights finally fixed their lock on the target with a lock. Meanwhile Shai observed the sparrows targeting lasers track up along his chest, but the reticle didn’t stop there; it kept rising up past Tex, past John, flickering through the billowing fog deeper into the tunnel where a deep recessed void appeared that hadn’t been there before.

“Storm Rail Charged” strobed in the top left of Tex’s HUD, Suddenly in a bright unison flash of blue and amber, the tunnel walls lit up in rapid succession. Blinding the others from both directions within milliseconds of the other. The Sparrow let loose it’s Kinetic rifle, Tex steadfast in his firing stance arched back slightly as a thick metal slug left the Storm-rails barrel. A tight crisp cloud of steam tailing it’s trail.

Tex felt a  percussive ripple fly through his suit, sending tingles down his spine. A scattered shock wave belted through the tunnel with a deafening disorienting effect. Adrenaline coursed through his body, sending tingles down his veins from head to toe. Tex closed his eyes, and thought of what it would be like to die, imagining the emptiness of it. He knew if he’d failed in his shot, the others wouldn’t stand a chance. He thought he was done for anyway, so he took the risk to save them, and he found comfort knowing they might make it out alive.

The Sparrow let out a howling bionic scream, jumbled static mixed with corrosive high pitched piezoelectric buzzing, gnawed at their skulls, seamlessly bypassing their suit’s built in decibel filters.

It stumbled uncontrollably, it’s steaming railgun aimlessly spinning about flagging the others in the process, snapped and twisted against the tunnel walls into spaghetti as it thrashed about helplessly. Eventually it plummeted into rock and snow sending debris flying deeper into the tunnel peppering it’s targets.

Tau gritted her teeth as she tweaked settings desperately to block out the frequencies. Finally the buzzing stopped, their ears still ringing with tinnitus as they reoriented. A softening static slipped from the tunnel as the machines last hum whispered down into the cold embracing of silence. For a split moment it felt like as though a ghost had escaped from its now lifeless armour cladded shell. It now laid peacefully blocking the tunnel entrance behind it.

Tex’s Storm-rail still had steam billowing from it’s glowing muzzle as it slowly found it’s resting place down his chest. His body like a ragdoll fell forward powerless, caught in a kneeling cradle hunched over his forward knee as he tried to move, but he felt no response. He could think of doing it, but his body remained still. His heavy head followed his chest dropping forward resting to the side against the shaft of the cooling Storm-rail. He gazed down at the ground, his thoughts began to wander aimlessly. The monstrosity clad in his oversized suit's thick armour knelt dead still, like a statue in the middle of the tunnel. The atmosphere from the entrance of the tunnel propelled forward like a small wave from the sparrows' impact. the waves of mist clashed around Tex, settling like a resting pool of fog by a sleeping obelisk, it rippled along his calves, kissing his lifeless hands gently. “Tex!!” A tear forced its way out of Shai’s eye straddling the bottom of her eye lid, filled with the internal blue glow from within her helmet, a small galaxy seemed to flicker within it as all the body functions of her teammates pulsed in a barrage of information. She wasn’t checking them, She wasn’t thinking, she was in a sea of rage and sorrow.

With Shai preoccupied and John still covering the front, Tau looked back through the thick fog at the rear of the tunnel. A burning blue glow caressed her gaze drawing her in. “John” Tau whispered  slowly, easing her way deeper toward the void. “There is something..” she switched her HUD to thermals “someone..  behind us”. “Get it together Shai” said John with sharp authority.

“OK, ok, ok cap”, Shai collected herself and began checking Tex’s vitals through her HUD. “I’m still picking up neural activity but it’s limited to involuntary functions, he’s still breathing”. John closed his eyes with a sigh of relief. “It’s locked in syndrome, His neural link was disconnected impromptu… from an EMP charge..” Said Shai.  “We took out that things fucking EMP!”, John’s voice tremored, he had done this as routine, he clawed in his mind at the possibility of a storm rail critical misfunction. “I’m tapping into his suit and initiating an emergency reboot”. Shai, was beginning to gain composure again.

Tex, groaned, moaning in discomfort, his eyes rolling from the back of his skull back to their resting place, druel dripped from his bottom lip. His jawline twitched as he observed a notification pulsing in his HUD. “Reboot initiated”. He felt the life pouring into the back of his neck like freezing water, then his shoulders, arms, torso, legs and eventually his toes. His body ached and burned buzzing and twitching, like a bed of needles pierced his soul as he urged himself forward, One knee up, then the next  he raised himself in agony from the ground.

“What the fuck..” Tex’s groaned in annoyance, as he locked his jaw back and forth regaining voluntary muscle control.. “That Sparrow take down … Nice work! I didn’t even hit the darn thing, I lost control of my arms just as I pulled the trigger,” his eyes drifted from what remained of a steaming splintered hulking wreck of the sparrow. His eyes climbed their way up the tunnels edge, eventually to find a watermelon sized cavity his stray shot had carved, the slug or what remained of it sitting proud in the middle of it. The cavity sat proud just above where the sparrow once hovered before it had dramatically met it’s end.

“Johnnn!!” Tau croaked with annoyance still trying to edge his attention. She had made her way to the rear of Tunnel, “You’re going to want to see this.” the sound of crushing ice and stone beneath her boots turned to a metallic thud. She knelt down, running her fingers through the ice and ruble to reveal an unnatural metallic floor.

Tex, realizing as his senses came too he was the only heavy gunner in the squad, turned about face throwing his storm-rail back on his shoulder it’s reticle now locked directly on the void. Silence took a hold of them as they locked sites at the end of the tunnel in anticipation. Slowly, a falling belly of fog and steam spilled endlessly through a wall that seemed to breathe. By now the blue glow that had drawn Tau in had diminished to nothing.

Suddenly a belly of fog and steam hurled toward them from as the breathing wall gave way, scattering their sensors and vision. A cloak field like that at the face of the cliff powered down revealing an unnatural structure behind it, seemingly organic yet also steel.

 They could hardly believe what they were seeing. An EMP cannon the size of a minibus had been hidden within the tunnel. It’s positioning  well planned. A defensive vantage point overlooking the tunnels opening, encapsulated behind a seamless cloaked wall with only an opening small enough to allow for the Cannons muzzle to sit ever so proudly, concealed behind the cloaking field which was no more.

The electric hum that had taken them by surprise eased down to a whispering static. Something was moving behind the turret, seated at it’s control centre. Immediately rifle sites raised at the mysterious figure to the rear of the cannon as they hugged the walls of the void closing distance between them.

“Waaaa hooooo!!, I’ve been waiting to use this bad boy for over a century now!”, A joyous victory chant filled the tunnel with a voice slightly inorganic. At John’s direction the others lowered their arms, Tex’s rifle still slightly raised untrusting. “A century yet before this cowboy leaves town you protectant genocidal bastards you!” Tau look
